name: MPT Narmada Resort (Temple View)
signature_dish: Pure-veg multi-cuisine dinner with Mandhata island view
why_it_matters: Madhya Pradesh Tourism's main property at Omkareshwar, on the mainland Mortakka side — the only mid-range hotel restaurant with line-of-sight to Mandhata Island (where the Omkareshwar Jyotirlinga sits). Pure-veg menu by design (Omkareshwar is non-veg-banned town-wide). The on-site restaurant is open to non-resident diners; reservations recommended Nov-Mar.
insider_tip: Reserve a temple-view facing table at sunset (6pm Oct-Mar, the temple lights come on by 6:15). Pure-veg only; no eggs either. The MPT property itself is a 5-min auto from the temple ghat — order an auto-back before 9:30pm or you'll wait. Skip Chinese on the menu; the kitchen's strength is the Indian veg side.
signature_address: MPT Temple View Omkareshwar (Narmada Resort), Overhead Water Tank, Mortakka-Omkareshwar Road, Omkareshwar, Madhya Pradesh 450554

name: Brahmin Bhojanalay
why_it_matters: One of Omkareshwar's most-named pilgrim-side veg dhabas on Mamleshwar Road, walking distance from the Mamleshwar Setu (the bridge linking the mainland to Mandhata Island). Sattvic cooking, no onion-garlic on request, the budget thali ₹150-250 default for families on the Jyotirlinga circuit. Cited in multiple holiday/restaurant aggregator pages as 'one of the most famous dhabas in Omkareshwar'.
insider_tip: Cash plus UPI. Crowded after the morning aarti (8-10am) and evening Bhasma aarti hours; window between 11am-1pm and 3pm-5pm is when you'll actually sit down without waiting. Pair with the Mamleshwar temple (the often-skipped 'second jyotirlinga' interpretation) which is 200m further down the same road.
signature_address: Mamleshwar Road, Omkareshwar H O, Khandwa District, Madhya Pradesh 450554

name: Omkar Prasadalay (Sansthan-run)
why_it_matters: Trust-run prasadalay built near the Mamleshwar Setu (the bridge to Mandhata Island) — the official affordable bhojan facility for Omkareshwar Jyotirlinga pilgrims, listed on the temple's own website (shriomkareshwar.org/Khanpan). Two strict slots: lunch 12-2pm, khichdi dinner 7-10pm. Sattvic preparation (no onion, no garlic, no root vegetables), nominal fee.
insider_tip: Strictly two windows, and outside them the kitchen is locked. The khichdi 7-10pm dinner is the better-quality slot (fresh-made). Carry your own bottled water — the prasadalay serves filtered local water by default. Closed during very rare temple-emergency days only.
signature_address: Near Mamleshwar Setu, Omkareshwar, Khandwa District, Madhya Pradesh 450554

name: Krishna Prasadam Restaurant
area: Near Omkareshwar Temple, Mandhata island side
why_it_matters: Pure-vegetarian sit-down restaurant near the Omkareshwar Temple ghat, serving the Indo-Chinese combo that family groups (especially with kids) usually need after a sattvic-only pilgrim day. Open 7am-10pm. The cleanliness rating from family-aggregator pages (MakeMyTrip TripIdeas, Tripadvisor) is consistently higher than the older bhojnalays.
insider_tip: Skip the noodles section on weekends — gets backed up. Veg thali is the easier order and the kitchen has it ready. Walk to the Omkar Mandhata temple after — Krishna Prasadam is 5 min on foot from the temple complex.
signature_address: Near Omkareshwar Temple, Mandhata island side, Omkareshwar, Khandwa District, Madhya Pradesh 450554
